newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland says to meet EMU deficit, debt goals in '9.
newsitem.headline: Finland says to meet EMU deficit, debt goals in '9.

text.p: Finland's public sector finances will fulfil the entry criteria for European economic and monetary union in 1997 and improve further next year, the finance ministry said on Tuesday in a new economic forecast.

The public sector deficit would narrow to 1.9 percent of GDP in 1997 from 2.6 percent last year while the gross public debt would rise to 58.7 percent of GDP this year from 58.0 percent in 1996, the ministry said in a statement.
The deficit criterion for EMU is at most three percent and the debt criterion is 60 percent. "Public finances will fulfil the EMU criteria," the ministry said.

"The entire public sector deficit is expected to fall below two percent of total production, and the public debt as defined by the requirements for EMU is likely to be under 60 percent of GDP this year," it said.

In 1998, "total public sector finances will be almost in balance owing to the surplus of the employment pension system. The ratio of public debt to GDP, as defined by the EMU criteria, will continue to fall," it said.
